Mike — thanks for the materials. Quick read/high-level comments:

1) Derivative-rights carveout
Your proposed clause excludes "derivative works" without sufficiently defining scope. Customers often interpret this to include transforms that we might need for debugging/repair. Suggest we:
- Limit the carveout to customer-created derivative works of their data only (i.e., outputs that are downstream productized by the customer).
- Add an explicit exception for ephemeral troubleshooting copies used by Redwood support under strict confidentiality.

2) Escrow-lite approach
An attested snapshot + runbook is reasonable for many customers, but procurement will want a guarantee for availability in certain termination scenarios. Consider: a staged escrow — snapshot + signed attestation stored with a neutral custodian, plus a documented activation checklist. I can share a short template.

3) Audit window / operator access
Two business days for a one-off audit is tight but acceptable if we limit scope to sample log extracts and read-only console evidence. If Canyon insists on hands-on operator exercises, we should define required insurance/forensics terms.

Can we have lauren and rishi take a pass on proposed alternate wording and share a mark-up? If so, I can compile a short redline memo for Canyon counsel.

Best,
Emily Chen
Senior Counsel, Lumen Law
